newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves, coupon pass expected.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves, coupon pass expected.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Tuesday through either customer or overnight system repurchase agreements, Fed watchers said.

"I'm looking for a customer RP today, but I'd not be surprised if the Fed does something more aggressive, such as an overnight system RP," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
By 0940 EST/1440 GTM, the federal funds rate was quoted at 5-7/16 percent, well above the central bank's 5-1/4 percent target.
Analysts did not discount the possibility of a Fed add move before the usual 1130 EST/1630 GMT intervention time, as has happened on occasion in recent sessions.
Analysts at consulting firm MMS International Inc. expect the Fed to inject reserves through system repurchase agreements on Tuesday.

Pundits are also expecting the Fed to add permanent reserves to the banking system on Tuesday through a coupon pass operation. "I'm expecting a coupon pass today ... I don't see much excuse for the Fed to delay that," Saporta said.

Analysts said it was difficult to predict the exact time the Fed may eventually intervene in the market. Historically, however, they said the Fed has carried out coupon passes any time between 1000 EST/1500 GMT to 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
